Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

old age noun

also in old age, in my old age, the old (old people collectively)

classical

Cic. Sen. 26: senectūs … sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid
Traupman 77

senectūs, senectūtis f.

noun, third declension; singular only

The ordinary word, and also old people as a group, as in senectūs semper agēns aliquid. Its opposite is adulēscentia.

Other words

  • senecta, senectae f. — old age

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.2.211: accēdente senectā; Traupman 77

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā post Augustum)

Examples

  • senectūs nōn modo languida atque iners nōn sit, vērum etiam sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid et mōliēns

    old age is not sluggish or idle, but busy, always doing and building somethingCic. Sen. 26

  • senectūs autem aetātis est perāctiō tamquam fābulae

    old age is the last act of life, as of a playCic. Sen. 85

  • Senectūs ipsa est morbus.

    Old age is itself a disease.Ter. Ph. 575

  • lēnior et melior fīs accēdente senectā?

    are you growing gentler and better as old age comes on?Hor. Ep. 2.2.211

See also old, grow old, age, youth, childhood.
